summary: Extract a shared src/shared/mcp-core.ts, byte-identical across context-keeper-remote / agentsync-remote / cambium-remote, guarded by a sha-256 drift test that all three repos pin to the same constant. A published package is the intended end state but deliberately deferred.
problem: Three remote MCP Workers each carried their own copy of the JSON-RPC envelope, the MCP handshake semantics, and a safeEqual token comparison. All three safeEqual copies carried the identical comment "kept in sync with the sibling Worker" and all three had nonetheless drifted to different behaviour within six weeks of first shipping: context-keeper-remote percent-decoded the path segment before comparing and the other two did not, and two of the three echoed the client's requested protocolVersion verbatim instead of validating it. A fourth Worker was foreseeable, so the copies had to be collapsed before the drift compounded further.
why_chosen: True sharing across three SEPARATE GitHub repos requires either a monorepo, a published npm package, or a git subtree — each of which needs an npm scope, a release workflow, and a coordinated version bump across three independent Cloudflare deploy pipelines. Doing that in the same pass as a batch of security fixes would have coupled an urgent, reviewable change to a risky infrastructure migration. Instead the code was collapsed into ONE import-free file (no imports, so it drops into any repo regardless of their differing extensionless-vs-.js module resolution) that is copied byte-identically, plus a test in each repo that hashes the file's LF-normalized bytes and compares against a constant pinned to the SAME value in all three. Editing the shared file in one repo turns that repo's suite red until the constant is updated, and updating the constant in only one repo makes the divergence visible in review. That converts drift from silent to loud, which was the actual failure mode, and it is reversible in one step once the package exists.
what_we_tried: Considered a monorepo (rejected: all three deploy independently to Cloudflare and are separately self-hostable/registry-listed), a git submodule or subtree (rejected: submodules break the one-click "Deploy to Cloudflare" fork flow these repos advertise), and simply re-syncing the copies by hand (rejected: that is exactly what the "kept in sync" comments already claimed to do, and it demonstrably failed).
tradeoffs: This is a drift DETECTOR, not real sharing: three files still exist and a determined editor can still update all three hashes without reconciling behaviour. It also adds a manual step to any shared-core edit (update the file and the hash in three repos in one PR). Accepted because the alternative was leaving three silently diverging security-critical copies in place for longer. A concrete TODO for the @xylem/mcp-core package end state is written at the top of mcp-core.ts.
constraints_created: src/shared/mcp-core.ts must stay import-free so it can be copied verbatim between repos with different module resolution
Any edit to src/shared/mcp-core.ts must update the pinned sha-256 in test/shared-drift.test.ts in ALL THREE repos in the same PR
Extract to a published @xylem/mcp-core package before a fourth remote Worker is created

summary: The remote Worker serves a read-only phone view at GET /view/<VIEW_TOKEN> -- server-rendered HTML, glance-shaped, on a SEPARATE credential from the MCP connector token -- and enriches it with cambium-remote's team/org knowledge counts via an optional CAMBIUM_STATUS_URL, fail-soft. VIEW_TOKEN unset means the route 404s, and each route refuses the other's token.
problem: The decision logs were only reachable from a desktop MCP client, and glancing at them on a phone had no path. The data was already remote (D1 holds 34 projects / 414 entries via the mirror), so the gap was presentation, not plumbing. But the obvious implementation -- reuse the connector URL -- is dangerous in a specific way this repo has already measured: AUTH_TOKEN is embedded in the URL and is read/write over every project, and the security section documents connector URLs appearing in ~54 places across 13 local transcripts on ONE machine. A dashboard URL is opened on a phone, where it lands in browser history, tab sync and screenshots, so reusing that token would place a full-write credential exactly where it leaks most, and rotating it to recover would break every claude.ai connector simultaneously.
why_chosen: A second, lower-value credential is the whole design. VIEW_TOKEN sits on a GET-only route that issues nothing but SELECTs, so a leaked glance-URL discloses decision summaries rather than write access to 34 projects. The separation is enforced in BOTH directions and tested as such -- /view rejects AUTH_TOKEN and /mcp rejects VIEW_TOKEN -- because a second credential that silently accepts the first is not a second credential. An unset VIEW_TOKEN 404s exactly like any unknown path, so the feature is off until deliberately enabled. Server-rendered rather than a client fetching JSON: the token never reaches JavaScript, there is no CORS surface, and the page works with scripting disabled. One document with inline CSS and zero external references -- on mobile data that is the difference between glanceable and not. Two D1 queries total rather than a fan-out per project. Entry text is arbitrary recorded prose being injected into HTML, so it is escaped and a test proves an summary renders inert. The cambium knowledge panel crosses a NETWORK boundary to a second Worker, so it is treated as an enrichment and never a dependency: bounded at 2.5s, kicked off before the D1 queries so the round trip overlaps rather than adds, and every failure mode (unset secret, timeout, non-200, unexpected shape) degrades to a stated absence rather than a blank space or a hung page. It sends an explicit User-Agent because context-keeper's con-007 records Cloudflare bot rules 403-ing a default client UA -- here that would present as a silently empty panel rather than an error. It shows team and org only: local scope is desktop-only by design AND is the staging area rather than the part that gets read (136 promoted items carry 774 recalls; 229 local ones carry 117), so the page states the absence instead of implying the counts are everything. cambium-remote's status performs no writes and its recall deliberately does not increment recall counters, so glancing from a phone cannot perturb the promotion signals the desktop side reasons about.
what_we_tried: Considered putting the view in cambium-remote (it holds team/org knowledge) or building a separate app. Rejected: context-keeper-remote already has the bulk of the data, the auth pattern and the deploy path, so a route here was the smallest thing that could work. Verified the rendered page at 375px in both colour schemes before shipping, via a stub D1 driving renderView outside the Worker -- the workerd test sandbox blocks filesystem writes, so capturing the HTML needed a path that did not go through vitest.
tradeoffs: Still a bearer secret in a URL, just a much cheaper one. Cloudflare Access in front of the route would remove the URL-credential class entirely and is free at this scale, but it is dashboard configuration rather than committable code. The feed is capped at 25 entries with no paging and no search -- deliberate for a glance surface, and the wrong shape if it ever becomes a working surface. The knowledge panel shows counts only, not items: cambium-remote's status is a cheap probe while recall would need a query, and a glance surface has nothing to query with. Setup now costs two secrets rather than one, and the second (CAMBIUM_STATUS_URL) embeds cambium-remote's own path token, so this Worker holds a credential for another -- acceptable because both are read-only surfaces of the same operator's data, but it is a real widening of what a compromise of this Worker would expose.

alternatives.reason_rejected: Puts a read/write credential for 34 projects into phone history, tab sync and screenshots -- the exact leak surface this repo already measured at ~54 occurrences. Rotating to recover would break every connector at once.

alternatives.option: Client-side fetch of the MCP JSON-RPC API
alternatives.reason_rejected: Puts the token in JavaScript, needs CORS on an endpoint that deliberately has none, and breaks with scripting off. Server rendering avoids all three.
The content spans private projects, so it could not be public; and a static page is stale the moment it is written, which defeats glancing.

alternatives.option: Cloudflare Access instead of a token
alternatives.reason_rejected: Strictly better security and free at this scale, but it is dashboard configuration rather than committable code. Worth adding on top of this later.

constraints_created: The view route must never fall back to AUTH_TOKEN, and /mcp must never accept VIEW_TOKEN. Tested in both directions.
Anything rendering recorded entry text into HTML must escape it -- the text is arbitrary prose from many sources.

summary: The view is enrolled once by token URL and used thereafter by a long-lived HttpOnly cookie, installed as a PWA. The cookie carries the same VIEW_TOKEN and is compared the same way, so there is exactly one revocation path and no server-side session state.
problem: Shipping /view/<VIEW_TOKEN> made the credential the user's problem. It is 43 characters, Cloudflare stores secrets write-only so it cannot be read back, and losing the clipboard meant re-running setup and invalidating the URL. For a page whose entire purpose is a ten-second glance on a phone, the handling cost exceeded the value of the thing being protected. The user's verdict was direct: it should be install-once, no keys, no passwords, nothing to remember.
why_chosen: Enrol-then-cookie moves the credential from the person to the device, which is what devices are for, without inventing an identity system. Reusing VIEW_TOKEN as the cookie value rather than minting a session id is the key property: revocation stays exactly one action (rotate the secret) and takes effect on the next request for every device at once. A session table would have created a second revocation path, and the one that gets forgotten is the one that stays valid. It also means no D1 writes, no expiry bookkeeping, and no state that can drift from the secret it represents. The PWA manifest points start_url and scope at the tokenless /view, so the installed icon is not a bookmark to a secret.
what_we_tried: First recommendation was OAuth (sign in with GitHub), and it was wrong: it requires the operator to register an OAuth app and configure a client id and client secret, which is more key handling, not less. It solves sharing with other people, which was not the problem. Cloudflare Access was also considered and rejected because it cannot sit in front of a workers.dev hostname without a custom domain. A hand-written QR encoder was written and abandoned after its output decoded to nothing under OpenCV; the qrcode package was then rejected because it pulls sharp and libvips with six high-severity advisories, to print text. qrcode-terminal has zero dependencies and its half-block output was verified scannable by decoding it.
tradeoffs: The cookie is a bearer credential with a ten-year lifetime, so a compromised device retains access until the token is rotated -- there is no per-device revocation, by design. Cookie loss (clearing site data) means re-enrolling from the QR or the saved URL. The URL is now stored at .view-url on disk, which is a persistent copy where previously there was none; that is the accepted cost of not requiring a person to hold a secret, and matches what npm, gh, aws and wrangler all do with their own tokens.

alternatives.option: GitHub or Google OAuth on the Worker
alternatives.reason_rejected: Requires registering an OAuth app and configuring a client secret, which is more credential handling for the operator, not less. Solves multi-user sharing, which was not the problem.

alternatives.option: Cloudflare Access in front of the route
alternatives.reason_rejected: Access applications are scoped to a zone you control; a workers.dev hostname is Cloudflare's zone, so this needs a custom domain first.

alternatives.option: Server-side session table in D1 with its own session ids
alternatives.reason_rejected: Creates a second revocation path that can disagree with the secret, plus expiry bookkeeping and a D1 write on every enrolment, to buy per-device revocation nobody asked for.

alternatives.option: Keep the token URL and just document bookmarking it
alternatives.reason_rejected: Leaves a live credential in browser history, sync, and every share sheet, and still requires transferring a 43-character secret by hand to reach a phone.

constraints_created: The cookie must never be accepted when VIEW_TOKEN is unset or empty; unset means the feature is off and must stay indistinguishable from an undeployed route
Literal /view asset paths must be routed before the /view/<token> pattern, since icon.png and manifest.webmanifest both match it
The manifest link must carry crossorigin=use-credentials or the manifest 404s behind the credential and the install prompt silently never appears
